issues.legal_issue: A delegated rule-making power limited to carrying out an enactment’s purposes does not authorize a transfer prohibition on land the enactment excludes from its operation when the prohibition is not contemplated by or in furtherance of the enactment.
material_facts: The enactment exempted tea estates, and its definition of a tea estate included other areas necessary for purposes subservient to a tea plantation.
A rule defined areas treated as subservient to tea plantations; an amendment added a prohibition on transferring such land without State Government permission.
A district registrar later directed registration officers not to register sale deeds for land exempted under the enactment.
The enactment did not express or imply an intention to prohibit transfers of the exempt land, which was not counted in determining surplus land or permissible holdings.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the transfer prohibition exceeded the delegated rule-making power and did not further the enactment’s purpose. It struck down the amended proviso and the implementing circular as invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 26 of the Himachal Pradesh Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1972, rules could be made to carry out the purposes of the Act; Sections 5(g) and the definition of “tea estate” placed tea estates, including qualifying subservient areas, outside its operation. Delegated legislation must conform to the parent statute and remain within the scope of the power conferred: Supreme Court Employees Welfare Association v. Union of India and General Officer Commanding-in-Chief v. Dr. Subhash Chandra Yadav. A general power to make rules for carrying out an Act’s purposes does not authorize the creation of substantive obligations or disabilities not contemplated by the Act; see Sant Saran Lal v. Parsuram Sahu. The Court also relied on the reasoning in Maharao Sahib Shri Bhim Singhji v. Union of India that a restriction on transfer of property outside the relevant ceiling controls could not be sustained.

predicates.challenge_to_delegated_rule_and_implemen: A party challenged a delegated rule and an administrative order implementing it.
predicates.land_category_excluded_from_enactment: The enactment excluded the relevant category of land from its operation.
predicates.general_rulemaking_power_limited_to_stat: The enactment authorized the government to make rules for carrying out the enactment’s purposes.
predicates.no_legislative_intent_to_control_transfe: The enactment contained no express or implied intention to control transfers of the excluded land.
predicates.transfer_bar_does_not_advance_enactment_: The transfer prohibition did not further the enactment’s purpose, and the land was not counted for its ceiling calculations.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a delegated rule and its implementing order, the land category is excluded from the enactment, and the enactment neither contemplates transfer controls nor benefits from them, the transfer restriction and implementing order are invalid.
